title.zh: 非洲旅遊的真實幻象：當「原真性」成為一場精心包裝的壯觀表演
title.en: The Spectacular Fantasy of African Tourism: When 'Authenticity' Becomes a Carefully Packaged Performance

summary.zh:
【總結】本文以南部非洲的卡萬戈-贊比西跨境保育區（KAZA）為案例，結合德波的「壯觀社會」理論與拉岡精神分析，揭示旅遊業如何透過「壯觀化」機制將「原真性」包裝成一種誘人的幻想。研究指出，這種幻想並非單純的誤導，而是透過選擇性呈現與不斷重複，創造出一種能持續刺激慾望、卻又永遠無法真正實現的消費體驗，進而產生一種矛盾性的「享樂」（jouissance）——一種夾雜痛苦與愉悅的深層心理滿足。

【研究問題】過去旅遊研究多聚焦於「原真性」的本質或主觀詮釋，卻較少探討媒體與行銷話語如何透過壯觀化機制塑造並維持這種幻想，以及其背後的權力不平等與政治生態學意涵。本研究旨在填補此空白，並解釋為何這種永遠無法實現的幻想反而具有如此強烈的吸引力。

【研究方法】作者採用批判性論述分析（CDA），系統性檢視KAZA相關十個主要利益相關者（包括德國联邦經濟合作部、KfW開發銀行、世界自然基金會德國/納米比亞/尚比亞分會、納米比亞旅遊局、尚比亞旅遊局、KAZA秘書處、和平公園基金會等）的官方網站、旅遊宣傳手冊與專案報告。資料蒐集時間為2025年6月至9月，涵蓋2004年至2025年的公開內容。分析過程透過主題編碼，聚焦於自然、文化、旅遊體驗與「做好事」四大主題，並比較各利益相關者敘述的 convergences 與 divergences。

【結果】研究識別出KAZA旅遊幻想的三大支柱：第一，「原始自然與異國文化他者」——宣傳材料將KAZA描繪為「真正的非洲」，卻抹除人類痕跡，並將當地社群（如桑人）浪漫化為「活博物館」中的傳統符號，忽視其政治主體性與當代生活複雜性。第二，「安全舒適的冒險」——旅遊宣傳同時強調刺激冒險與極致舒適，創造出一個「旅遊泡泡」，讓遊客在無風險的前提下消費「危險」，卻掩蓋了當地人必須面對的真實生存風險。第三，「做好事的幻覺」——旅遊被包裝成保育、社區發展與經濟成長的雙贏方案，但實際上，博茨瓦納超過70%的旅遊收入回流至外國母公司，納米比亞赞比西地區僅約20%的旅遊價值被當地吸收，且多數高端遊客直接入住偏遠豪華營地，幾乎不消費當地經濟。這些矛盾透過壯觀化被掩蓋，持續刺激遊客的慾望與享樂，同時再生產了新殖民主義的權力階序。
summary.en:
**Summary:** This article examines the Kavango Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area (KAZA) in southern Africa, combining Debord's theory of the spectacle with Lacanian psychoanalysis to reveal how the tourism industry packages 'authenticity' into an alluring fantasy through spectacularization. The study argues that this fantasy is not mere deception but a carefully constructed mechanism that selectively presents and endlessly repeats images, generating a desire that can never be fully satisfied—producing a contradictory form of jouissance, a deep psychological pleasure intertwined with pain.

**Problem:** While tourism studies have extensively debated the nature and subjectivity of authenticity, they have largely overlooked how media and promotional discourses spectacularize and sustain this fantasy, along with the underlying power inequalities and political ecological implications. This article addresses that gap, explaining why an inherently unattainable fantasy exerts such powerful appeal.

**Approach:** The authors employ Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) to systematically examine the official websites, tourism brochures, and project reports of ten key KAZA stakeholders: the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), KfW development bank, WWF Germany/Namibia/Zambia, Namibia Tourism Board, Zambia Tourism, the KAZA Secretariat, and Peace Parks Foundation. Data collected between June and September 2025 spanned materials from 2004 to 2025. Through thematic coding focused on nature, culture, tourist experience, and 'doing good,' the analysis mapped convergences and divergences across stakeholder narratives.

**Results:** The study identifies three pillars of KAZA's tourism fantasy. First, 'pristine nature and exotic cultural others'—promotional materials depict KAZA as 'the real Africa' while erasing human presence, romanticizing local communities (such as the San) as living museum relics, and ignoring their political agency and contemporary complexities. Second, 'safe and comfortable adventure'—marketing simultaneously sells thrilling danger and luxury comfort, creating a 'tourist bubble' that lets visitors consume risk without consequence, while obscuring the real dangers local people face daily. Third, the 'illusion of doing good'—tourism is framed as a win-win for conservation and community development, yet over 70% of Botswana's tourism revenue repatriates to foreign parent companies, and only about 20% of tourism value in Namibia's Zambezi region stays local. High-end tourists bypass local economies entirely, staying in remote luxury camps. These contradictions are spectacularized away, sustaining desire and jouissance while reproducing neo-colonial hierarchies.

keyArticle.title: Enjoying contradictions: The spectacular fantasy of tourism authenticity in southern Africa
